tagline: Gravel through basalt country gives way to a river gorge
intro: Highway 27 winds 43 miles north from Highway 20 to Prineville on the Lower Crooked River Back Country Byway. The southern 18 miles are graded gravel suitable for passenger vehicles, crossing a landscape of private ranches, public rangeland, rolling hills and basalt buttes. BLM’s byway description pairs that open country with the gorge of the Crooked Wild and Scenic River, where campgrounds, day-use areas and a hiking trail line the river. The entire route remains a state highway.

The river corridor changed in 1961 when the Bureau of Reclamation built Bowman Dam. Its reservoir flooded a canyon of juniper and sagebrush as part of the Crooked River Project. Irrigation storage was the primary purpose, with flood control and recreation secondary. The dam took the name of Arthur Ray Bowman, a Prineville businessman who had supported the project. Behind the dam, Prineville Reservoir extends along 18 miles of the Crooked River, storing water upstream of the drive through the gorge.

Driving north, reach pavement before crossing Bowman Dam’s spillway and descending into the Chimney Rock river segment. Chimney Rock rises above the highway opposite its namesake campground. The drive finishes in Prineville, where the Bowman Museum occupies the old Crook County Bank building.

moments.title: Bowman Dam
moments.text: Bowman Dam marks the road’s transition into the river gorge: the byway crosses its spillway before descending into the Chimney Rock segment. This earth dam holds Prineville Reservoir on the Crooked River. The Bureau of Reclamation constructed it in 1961, and the Ochoco Irrigation District operates it. Upstream, the reservoir occupies what was a canyon filled with juniper and sagebrush. Water storage for irrigation leads its purposes, followed by flood control and recreation. The name honors Arthur Ray Bowman, who helped establish the Ochoco Irrigation District and took a particular interest in building the dam.
moments.notice: The byway crosses the dam’s spillway before descending into the Crooked River gorge.

moments.title: Chimney Rock
moments.text: Chimney Rock stands above Highway 27, opposite Chimney Rock Campground. A 1.3-mile trail climbs to the butte from the trailhead across the highway. It is part of a river corridor with nine year-round campgrounds and two day-use areas. BLM identifies camping, fishing and hiking as year-round opportunities along this stretch of the Crooked Wild and Scenic River.
moments.notice: Look for the butte above the highway, opposite Chimney Rock Campground.

moments.title: Bowman Museum
moments.text: Bronze teller cages and marble counters remain inside the Bowman Museum, which occupies Prineville’s former Crook County Bank. The two-story building was constructed in 1910 with stone from a local quarry west of the Ochoco Viewpoint. Arthur Bowman bought the building for his title and insurance business after Prineville National Bank became insolvent during the Great Depression. His wife and two daughters donated it to Crook County in 1971 for use as a museum. The banking rooms now hold exhibits on the local railroad and timber industry, with historic photographs, furniture and tools alongside the original teller fittings.
